text: Catherine Christine Cowie is an American epidemiologist who serves as a program director and senior advisor in the Division of Diabetes, Endocrinology, and Metabolic Diseases at the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK). She earned a master of public health from the University of Michigan School of Public Health in 1979 and completed her Ph.D. at the same institution, working as a research associate and graduate teaching assistant from 1981 to 1988. Her dissertation, titled "Racial disparity in diabetic end-stage renal disease: trends in incidence, survival and possible explanatory factors," was supervised by Victor M. Hawthorne. From 1979 to 1981, she worked as an epidemiologist at Upjohn, and from 1988 to 1996, she served as an epidemiologist at the NIDDK, focusing on social and scientific systems. Cowie directs programs in diabetes epidemiology and is responsible for the scientific oversight of the Diabetes Control and Complications Trial/Epidemiology of Diabetes Interventions and Complications study (DCCT/EDIC). Her duties include managing diabetes epidemiology interests such as developing national survey components, analyzing and publishing data, mentoring epidemiologists, and directing computer programmers. She chairs the NIDDK Epidemiology Group Committee and has edited the books *Diabetes in America* and *Diabetes Public Health: From Data to Policy*. Currently, she manages the development and analysis for the third edition of *Diabetes in America*. She represents the NIDDK on the National Diabetes Statistics Report and participates in various HHS diabetes epidemiology projects. Cowie is also a member of multiple trans-NIDDK, NIH, and HHS committees related to clinical and epidemiologic research. In June 2018, she was awarded the American Diabetes Association Kelly West Award for Outstanding Achievement in Epidemiology for her significant contributions to diabetes epidemiology.
